question.text: Ritu, a salaried employee with a basic salary of Rs.8,00,000 per annum, works for a private company. Her employer contributes Rs.1,20,000 (15% of salary) to NPS on her behalf. Under Section 80CCD(2) and the new tax regime, what deduction is available to Ritu?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under Section 80CCD(2), the employer's contribution to NPS is allowed as a deduction in the hands of the employee. For private-sector employees, the workbook caps the deduction at 14% of salary under the new tax regime (and 10% of salary under the old regime). Ritu's salary is Rs.8,00,000, so 14% = Rs.1,12,000. The employer contributed Rs.1,20,000, but only Rs.1,12,000 is deductible; the excess Rs.8,000 is not allowed. The Trap: Option A allows the full 15% employer contribution without applying the 14% ceiling. Option B uses the 10% old-regime cap, which is not what the question asks. Option D uses an invented 5% rate. Note: If the same fact pattern were tested under the old regime, the cap would be 10% of salary = Rs.80,000. Under the new regime, 14% of salary = Rs.1,12,000.
